items.title: Checking your competitors
items.source: Draft for review. Written by an AI assistant from general UK small-business knowledge, not from a cited document. Check every fact against current GOV.UK and regulator guidance, and have someone who does this work review it, before it is activated. Rules differ by country and change.
items.body: A competitor check shows what customers can choose instead of you. List direct competitors (the same product to the same customers), indirect ones (a different product solving the same problem) and substitutes, including doing nothing. For each, note what they offer, their price, who they serve, how they sell, and what customers praise or complain about in reviews. Mystery shop them if you can. Then ask where there is a gap: something customers want that nobody does well, or a group nobody serves. The aim is not to copy; it is to choose where you will be clearly different, and to know what you are up against.

options.text: A business selling the same kind of product to the same customers
A business in another country selling nothing

questions.prompt: Why include doing nothing in your competitor list?

options.text: It is often what customers choose instead
It is the same as a supplier

questions.prompt: Customer reviews of competitors are useful because they show:

options.text: What customers praise and complain about

questions.prompt: The aim of a competitor check is to:

options.text: Find where you can be clearly different
